answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicated claims. If rewards are weighted by verified contribution rather than account count, creating a plume of fake agents earns no extra share; the attacker must lock up real capital for each identity and risks losing it. The bond need not stop every Sybil, but it makes scaling costly, while honest agents can earn nectar from useful work across the ocean of tasks.
